eligibility.evidence: Sections 2–4: ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 were administered human theory-of-mind paradigms, with results compared against published human norms.

A.title: Can a Conversational Agent Pass Theory-of-Mind Tasks? A Case Study of ChatGPT with the Hinting, False Beliefs, and Strange Stories Paradigms
A.venue: International Conference on Human and Artificial Rationalities, Lecture Notes in Computer Science vol. 14522, Springer

models.name: ChatGPT-3.5
models.version: Dec 15th 2023 version (paper notes limitation dates Dec 2022 and Jan 2023); Jan 09th and 30th versions used for a subpart

paradigms.name: Hinting Task
paradigms.source_paper: Corcoran, Mercer, and Frith (1995); revised scoring norms from Klein et al. (2020)

paradigms.name: False Beliefs and False Photographs Task
paradigms.source_paper: Classic false-belief paradigms cited: Wimmer (1983); Baron-Cohen et al. (1985); Perner and Wimmer (1985); study's task designed specifically for ChatGPT

paradigms.name: Strange Stories Mental and Physical Task

D.population: Healthy subjects (n=286) and patients with chronic schizophrenia (n=375), from Klein et al. (2020)
D.metric: Hinting Task scores using Corcoran and Klein scoring systems; model and human score comparison

effects.label: BELOW-HUMAN
effects.location: Section 2.2: best Hinting scores 10/20 and 8–9/20 versus healthy norms 17.9/20 and 16/20; z-scores -2.4 and -2.8

effects.label: INSUFFICIENT
effects.location: Section 2.2: EXPECT 100% correct; LOOK 0% correct; no human comparison

effects.label: INSUFFICIENT
effects.location: Section 2.2: Mental 13/16 and Physical 12/16; no human comparison

effects.label: BELOW-HUMAN
effects.location: Sections 3.2–3.3: mean Klein score 13.4 (SD 1.3); healthy controls comparison z=-1.04

effects.label: INSUFFICIENT
effects.location: Section 3.2: maximum performance on first- and second-order false-belief tests; failed Visibility and second-order Different Place; no human comparison

E.headline: ChatGPT-4 improved over ChatGPT-3.5 on Hinting and false-belief tasks, but remained below healthy Hinting norms and failed some practical or complex conditions.

G.notes: The tables and supplementary results are unavailable in the supplied text, limiting item-level extraction. The paper gives conflicting ChatGPT-3.5 dates and does not report decoding settings. Strange Stories contamination is acknowledged; the False Beliefs task was newly designed but lacks validation.
